article.title: Robert Nadeau (aikidoka)
article.coi: The requester personally knows Robert Nadeau; the research project holds his recollections of Nadeau-era dojos as graph evidence (kkron://personal-communication/*) — disclosed for transparency, never used as a source.

gng.note: Live article exists; 19 RELIABLE sources per regenerated reliability report.

items.claim: Nadeau taught in the Soviet Union — a training at the Lenkai Aikido Club in Leningrad on October 27, 1990, the day of the USSR Aikido Federation founding conference; he held 6th dan. Live article's taught-countries list omits Russia.

evidence.note: V. Matveev, Moscow Aiki Club history of St. Petersburg aikido (2003) — names 'Robert NADO (6 dan, USA)' at Lenkai on 27 Oct 1990, invited by Moscow aikidoka contemporaneous organizational record — usable attributed for date/place
Lenkai club's own archive — host venue is a participant, not a third party contemporaneous organizational record — usable attributed for date/place

Federal Alliance of Bujutsu Russia (Kazan) — recalls training with Nadeau 1987–1994; errs on nationality (Canada) — flag, don't silently fix contemporaneous organizational record — usable attributed for date/place
Same Kazan federation, second web property — also says 7th dan (discrepancy recorded) contemporaneous organizational record — usable attributed for date/place
BigRock Aikikai interview with Jamie Zimron — corroborates the 1987–1991 exchange period, not Nadeau specifically contemporaneous organizational record — usable attributed for date/place
Kannagara Aikido Moscow — Barrish timeline context contemporaneous organizational record — usable attributed for date/place

items.rationale: Contemporaneous primary records of a scheduled event — usable for date/location/rank facts under WP:PRIMARY, but not independent journalism; significance claims still need secondary sourcing. Open question left to editors.

proposal.wikitext: According to the Moscow Aiki Club's history of aikido in St. Petersburg, Nadeau also taught in the Soviet Union, conducting a training at the [[Lenkai]] Aikido Club in [[Leningrad]] (now [[Saint Petersburg]]) on October 27, 1990 — the day of the founding conference of the USSR Aikido Federation. At the time of the visit, Nadeau held the rank of 6th [[dan (rank)|dan]].<ref name="aikiclub-spb">{{cite web | url = http://www.aikiclub.ru/spb.html | title = Развитие Айкидо в Санкт-Петербурге (Development of Aikido in St. Petersburg) | author = V. Matveev | publisher = Moscow Aiki Club | date = 2003-01-13 | language = ru | access-date = 2026-09-24 | quote = 27 октября 1990 года, в день проведения Учредительной конференции Федерации Айкидо СССР, в клубе "Ленкай" провел тренировку Роберт НАДО (6-й Дан, США), посетивший Советский Союз по приглашению айкидок из Москвы.}}</ref> The Lenkai Aikido Club, whose founder Sergey Kiselev was the first president of the USSR Aikido Federation, maintains an archival record of the visit.<ref name="lenkai-spb">{{cite web | url = https://lenkai.spb.ru/ajkido-v-sssr/ | title = Айкидо в СССР (Aikido in the USSR) | author = Sergey Kiselev | publisher = Lenkai Aikido Club, St. Petersburg | language = ru | access-date = 2026-09-24}}</ref> The visit occurred amid a broader exchange between American and Soviet aikidoka in the late 1980s and early 1990s; instructors from the Federal Alliance of Bujutsu Russia in Kazan also recall training with Nadeau during this period.<ref name="bujutsu-aikido">{{cite web | url = https://bujutsu.ru/aikido/ | title = Айкидо — Федерация Боевых Искусств России | publisher = Federal Alliance of Bujutsu Russia | language = ru | access-date = 2026-09-24}}</ref>

rationale_blocks.title: Sourcing rationale for the Russian-language records (for the talk page)
rationale_blocks.body: The four Russian-language sources are contemporaneous primary records of scheduled events, not promotional material: (1) aikiclub.ru/spb.html — Moscow Aiki Club history, names 'Robert NADO (6th dan, USA)' at the Lenkai club on the day of the USSR Aikido Federation founding conference, Oct 27 1990; (2) bujutsu.ru — Kazan federation recalls training under Nadeau 1987–1994 (erroneously lists Canada); (3) rebenok-na-aikido.ru — same org's second property, 7th-dan variant (discrepancy recorded); (4) lenkai.spb.ru — the host venue's own archive (participant, not third party). WP:PRIMARY: used only for date/location/rank/fact-of-event — no analytical claims. No better source identified: no English-language journalism, Aikido Journal, or Hombu records of these seminars found (30+ Russian-language queries documented in docs/nadeau-russia-seminar-search.md).
